note: Three axes: technical domain x role function x organizational context. Job titles are aliases for combinations, and none of the axes produces a ranking. This file is where changes are made. The eight axes, two scales and four levels use the same values as the Mechanical Engineering Core: results from two majors can only be compared on the same ruler, and building a new ruler for each major would break comparison within a university

J1.name: Problem definition
J1.question: Who decided what to work on?

J2.name: Requirements interpretation
J2.question: Did you turn the requirements into numbers and constraints?

J3.name: Technical decisions
J3.question: Which items did you decide yourself?

J4.name: Methods and tools
J4.question: What did you use, and how?

J6.name: Comparison and verification
J6.question: What did you compare it against?

J7.name: Failure and correction
J7.question: How did you narrow down what went wrong?

J8.name: Organizational use
J8.question: Who used it, and for what?

S4.note: Screening scale. The four axes asked at BASIC. Organizational use is left out of screening because it puts undergraduates at a structural disadvantage: whether your work was used by an organization can only be answered if you were placed in one, and someone who has only done classes and a capstone will have that cell empty even if they made decisions. Organizational use is asked only in the in-depth stage

S8.note: Full scale. STANDARD and above. Do not use S8 as the denominator for S4. What the in-depth stage newly opens are the four axes not in screening (problem definition, requirements interpretation, methods and tools, organizational use)

levels.L1: Exposed. Watched or reused what someone else did
levels.L3: Owned. Decided it myself, and the result was used

technical_domains.owns: Decides what to communicate to whom

technical_domains.name: Message and Concept

technical_domains.name: Media and Channel Planning
technical_domains.owns: Decides where, how much and how to release
subareas: What to change for each channel

technical_domains.name: Cinematography and Lighting Design
technical_domains.owns: Decides what to capture with which light and angle
subareas: What to capture and what to drop

technical_domains.name: Sound and Audio
technical_domains.owns: Decides the sound that is heard

technical_domains.name: Directing, Structure and Script
technical_domains.owns: Decides in what order to show things

technical_domains.name: Editing and Post-production
technical_domains.owns: Turns the footage into one version to release

role_functions.name: Planning and Structure
role_functions.one_line: Decides what to make and how
role_functions.success: One complete set that states what to say to whom and that other people can produce as it is

role_functions.name: Research and Analysis
role_functions.one_line: Finds out what can be known before making something
role_functions.output_kind: Audience research records · Media data · Case analysis
role_functions.success: A record that states the range looked at and the data used, so the next person can look at it again in the same way

role_functions.name: Judgment and Review Response
role_functions.one_line: Checks whether work can be released
role_functions.output_kind: Review opinion · Inspection records · Transmission check records
role_functions.success: A result where the judgment fits review standards and specifications and the range looked at is written down

role_functions.name: Records and Standards Management
role_functions.one_line: Leaves records and standards so that anyone gets the same result
role_functions.output_kind: Production manual · Material list and versions · Transmission specification table
role_functions.success: The same specifications give the same result, and it is possible to go back to any version

role_functions.name: Production Site
role_functions.one_line: Makes the output come out on the spot
role_functions.output_kind: Shooting records · Cue sheet · What was changed that day and the reasons
role_functions.success: It runs to the end that day, and changes remain in the records

role_functions.name: Operations and Coordination
role_functions.one_line: Ties many people's decisions into one
role_functions.output_kind: Schedule · Booking and contract records · Change records
role_functions.success: Meeting deadlines, successful bookings and the number of breaks

role_functions.name: Survey and Research
role_functions.one_line: Narrows down things that have no answer yet
role_functions.output_kind: Effect measurement design and data · Case studies · Indicator definitions
role_functions.success: The question is narrowed down, and a record remains that allows the work to be done again

role_functions.name: Rights and Regulation Management
role_functions.one_line: Makes sure standards are kept all the time
role_functions.output_kind: Rights check records · Review response records · Safety plan
role_functions.success: The same disputes and accidents do not come back, and the basis of decisions can be traced

role_functions_note: There are eight, and they use **the same codes** as the Mechanical Engineering Core. Role functions are a layer above the major, so they are not created again for each major. The names were changed into the words of media, advertising and performance majors. The meaning of the work is kept the same, so the axes do not split; what differs is the kind of output: outlines, cue sheets and transmission specifications take the place of mechanical drawings

org_contexts.name: Advertising Agencies and Production Companies
org_contexts.performance: Proposal adoption · Run deadlines · Advertiser approval
org_contexts.differs: If the advertiser does not choose an option, it does not survive

org_contexts.name: Broadcasters and Production Studios
org_contexts.performance: Scheduled air time · Viewing and views · Review
org_contexts.differs: Scheduled air time cannot be delayed

org_contexts.name: Performance Agencies and Theaters
org_contexts.differs: Once the curtain rises, nothing can be undone

org_contexts.name: Corporate Public Relations and Communication Teams
org_contexts.performance: Press reactions · Crisis response · Internal agreement
org_contexts.differs: One sentence becomes the company's words

org_contexts.name: Universities and Research Institutes
org_contexts.differs: You check on your own whether the method is right and keep it as a record

org_contexts.name: Platform and Content Operators
org_contexts.differs: The numbers after posting decide the next episode

org_contexts.name: Freelance and Solo Production
org_contexts.differs: One person plans, shoots, edits and delivers
